title: Grafana 13.3 Adds Shared Dashboard Variables and Notebooks
gist: Grafana 13.3 previews cross-dashboard variables (global or folder scope) and Notebooks for incident investigations, adds Grafana Assistant dashboard plans and a GA Undo turn, and previews a non-breaking visual refresh. Notebooks put Grafana in direct feature competition with Datadog and New Relic notebooks.

insights.claim: Grafana 13.3 introduces cross-dashboard variables in public preview across all editions, letting teams define a variable such as environment or region once and reuse it across multiple dashboards to avoid configuration drift.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Reduces dashboard sprawl maintenance for large Grafana deployments; strengthens Grafana's enterprise manageability story.
insights.locator: The release announcement describes cross-dashboard variables

insights.claim: Cross-dashboard variables answer a longstanding Grafana user request dating at least to a 2021 GitHub discussion, where a user warned separately maintained variables could become unmanageable over time.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Shows Grafana closing multi-year usability gaps, which matters for retention against commercial rivals.
insights.locator: Cross-dashboard variables address a longstanding user request

insights.claim: Grafana shared variables can be globally scoped across an organisation or folder-scoped, with configuration centrally managed while viewers can still change selected values; an early tester found them useful for evaluating Git Sync without Terraform templating.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Native sharing reduces reliance on Terraform templating for dashboard-as-code workflows.

insights.claim: Self-managed Grafana users must enable the grafana.dashboardGlobalVariables feature toggle to try cross-dashboard variables, managed under Dashboards > Variables.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Feature remains preview-gated for self-hosted users.
insights.locator: Teams running Grafana themselves must enable

insights.claim: Grafana 13.3 Notebooks, in public preview across all editions, combine panels from dashboards or Explore with written observations and Grafana Assistant findings, for recording investigations or preparing post-incident reviews.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Moves Grafana into incident-investigation workflows where Datadog and New Relic already compete.
insights.locator: Notebooks are also in public preview

insights.claim: Grafana is rolling Notebooks out gradually to Grafana Cloud, while self-managed installations need the dashboard.notebooks feature toggle; notebooks can be created manually or via Grafana Assistant.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Cloud-first rollout reflects Grafana Labs' push toward its hosted offering.
insights.locator: Users can create a notebook manually

insights.claim: Grafana's Notebooks follow similar features from Datadog Notebooks, which offer simultaneous editing, inline comments and postmortem templates, and New Relic Notebooks, generally available since August 2026 with NRQL queries, natural-language query translation and notebook-wide variables.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Investigation notebooks are becoming table stakes in observability; competitive differentiation shifts to AI assistance.
insights.locator: Grafana's Notebooks joins similar investigation-document workflows

insights.claim: Grafana Assistant dashboard plans, in public preview, let a user describe what to monitor and review a proposed layout with title, panels, visualisation types and variables in chat and a read-only preview before building it.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: AI-generated dashboards with human review lowers the skill barrier to Grafana adoption.
insights.locator: The release also changes how Grafana Assistant builds dashboards

insights.claim: Grafana Assistant's Undo turn is generally available across all editions, restoring the previous dashboard state after an Assistant edit even if it changed multiple panels, but it is unavailable if the dashboard has changed since the edit.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Reversibility controls are becoming a standard requirement for AI agents that edit production artifacts.
insights.locator: A separate Assistant feature, Undo turn

insights.claim: Grafana 13.3 previews a visual refresh of themes and interface components that Grafana Labs says preserves navigation and workflows with no breaking changes for plugins; plugins using standard components and theme tokens inherit the new look while custom-styled plugins can migrate separately.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Non-breaking UI refresh limits ecosystem disruption for plugin vendors.
insights.locator: Grafana 13.3 also previews a visual refresh
